question_text: Distinguish between red muscle fibers and white muscle fibers.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Red muscle fibres
steps.why: Myoglobin stores oxygen and mitochondria use it, so a fibre rich in both can keep working without tiring.
common_mistakes: Calling red fibres anaerobic. They are aerobic.
Leaving out myoglobin, which is what makes them red.
steps.memory_tip: Red means more myoglobin, more mitochondria, aerobic work.
lines: Red muscle fibres have more myoglobin and
They use the oxygen stored in myoglobin,

steps.label: White muscle fibres
steps.why: With little stored oxygen the fibre must release energy without it, which is fast but tires quickly.
common_mistakes: Giving white fibres more mitochondria. They have very few.
steps.memory_tip: White means less myoglobin, few mitochondria, anaerobic work.
lines: White muscle fibres have less myoglobin

insider_note: Myoglobin is what makes the fibre red, so name it first: more myoglobin and more mitochondria, then the word aerobic. Mirror the same three points for white fibres.
